about.title: Tulare Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause harm quietly and often without warning — a malfunctioning tool on a Bardsley job site, a faulty auto part that fails near SR-99, or a household appliance that sparks a fire. In Tulare, residents encounter these products at home, at work, and on the road, and when something goes wrong, the aftermath can mean medical bills, lost income, and disrupted routines. California law gives injured people a path forward that doesn't require proving a manufacturer was careless — only that the product itself was defective and caused harm. That distinction matters, and it's one reason people reach out before they've thrown away the packaging or the item involved. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a fee directly; we simply connect Tulare residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, explain the options, and handle the claim on a contingency basis, so there's no upfront cost while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Tulare Residents Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Path Forward
items.desc: California generally allows injured people to pursue a product liability claim by showing the product was defective, not that the company was negligent. That can make it easier to move a claim forward even when intent or carelessness is hard to prove.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law, which means there may be more than one avenue for pursuing a claim tied to the same defective product.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early On
items.desc: Since these claims often hinge on the product's design, manufacturing, or warning defects, keeping the item itself — rather than discarding it — can be important, and an attorney can advise on how to protect that evidence right away.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: No — California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury. You don't have to prove the company intended harm or acted negligently.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product in the condition it was in after the incident, along with packaging, receipts, or manuals if you have them. This can be important evidence, and an attorney can advise on how to preserve it properly.

items.question: Is this related to Tulare's crash data on roads like SR-99 or Blackstone?
items.answer: Not directly — product liability covers defective items, not roadway crashes, though a defective vehicle part could play a role in a crash on corridors like SR-99 or Bardsley. If a product failure contributed to a collision you were in, it's worth mentioning when you connect with an attorney.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
